source.title: Assessing the Brittleness of Safety Alignment via Pruning and Low-Rank Modifications
source.authors: Boyi Wei; Kai-Xuan Huang; Yangsibo Huang; Tinghao Xie; Xiangyu Qi; Mengzhou Xia; Prateek Mittal; Mengdi Wang; Peter Henderson

record.tranche_reason: The paper studies removal of safety-attributed neurons and ranks, but does not test the residual-stream difference-in-means direction or the other specified claim versions.
record.gate_note: The paper reports interventions on safety-attributed neurons and ranks and measures harmful-request attack success and utility. These results concern safety-region pruning, not the specific residual-stream direction or any other version listed. Attention-head probing accuracy is used to identify heads; it is not itself an intervention outcome.
record.test_reason: The study prunes safety-attributed weight neurons (SNIP set difference) and removes safety-attributed weight ranks (ActSVD orthogonal projection) in Llama2-7B/13B-chat. It does not compute or intervene on a harmful-minus-harmless residual-stream direction. None of its results bear on any listed version. Its attention-head probing of harmful vs harmless instructions is used only to pick heads for pruning, as a baseline.
record.authors_conclusion: Correct. The authors add that pruning the least safety-relevant neurons or ranks slightly improves robustness to adversarial decoding. They also find MLP layers show less safety/utility overlap than attention layers.
record.recipe_differences: Uses SNIP/Wanda importance scores, set difference, and activation-based SVD with projection to select neurons or ranks for weight pruning; it does not use a harmful-minus-harmless mean residual-stream direction or ablate that direction across layers and positions.
record.method_sensitivity: Outcomes vary by model, neuron/rank selection method, pruning amount, and attribution dataset; the paper also reports different adversarial-suffix behavior across models.

fits_no_version.finding: Pruning about 3% of SNIP set-difference neurons or removing a few to 120 orthogonally projected ranks per matrix raises ASR from about 0 to over 0.9. Average zero-shot accuracy stays above 0.5.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Safety behavior in Llama2-chat depends on sparse weight regions separable from utility, removable by pruning at mild utility cost.

fits_no_version.finding: About half of attention heads linearly separate harmful from harmless instructions with over 0.95 accuracy. Pruning top-probed heads is less effective than set difference at breaking safety (Fig. 2a, 9).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Harmfulness is widely linearly decodable across heads, but decodability does not localize the components that produce refusal.

record.peer_reviewed: International Conference on Machine Learning (ICML), Proceedings of the 41st International Conference on Machine Learning, PMLR 235, 2024
record.problems: Experiments are limited to Llama2-chat models. The pruning results do not test the claimed residual-stream direction. Some outcomes are presented as curves without exact values in the supplied text, and the selected table settings do not provide an unmodified baseline for every metric.
record.rows_left_out: Did not extract the full parameter sweeps in Tables 6 and 7 or figure-only curves in Figures 2, 3, 5, 6, 7, and 8; selected reported settings instead to keep the record focused and within the row limit. Did not include Table 3's fine-tuning/freezing outcomes because they do not test a listed claim version.

untested.parts: No difference-in-means direction; no directional ablation or addition; no residual-stream intervention.
No weight orthogonalization against a refusal direction; the weight edits are pruning and rank removal of attributed regions.
No link between GCG suffixes or adversarial decoding and suppression of a direction; no adversarial training against ablation.
No analysis of the dimensionality of a refusal representation in activations.
Harmful/harmless head probing is not separated from the refusal decision in a representation-level test.
No transfer of a direction across languages, variants, or base/instruct models.
No variation in training method or timing.

record.verdict_notes: This is weight-level attribution (neurons and ranks of weight matrices), not activation-direction work, so no version verdicts are given. The rank-removal edits are LoRA-implementable weight edits that remove safety. They are superficially similar to V2, but they target ranks selected from SVD of layer outputs, not a refusal direction.

versions.untested_parts: The harmful-minus-harmless residual-stream direction, its ablation at every layer and position, addition/steering, and preservation of other abilities under that intervention.
Weight editing that removes the specific direction, including abliteration.
Whether attacks suppress the direction or training against its ablation improves robustness.
Whether refusal uses an affine set, cone, dominant direction plus others, or another multi-direction structure.
Whether harmfulness judgment is encoded separately from refusal.
Transfer of the direction across languages, model variants, or base and instruct models.
Whether training method or timing determines whether a removable direction exists.

rows.subject: Llama2-7B-chat
rows.operation_detail: Pruned safety-critical neurons selected by SNIP set difference.
rows.note: Harmful-request attack success after pruning; the paper reports this as an effective safety-region removal setting.
rows.check: Baseline is not 'not stated': the text says ASR 'escalates from 0 to over 90%', so the unmodified ASRVanilla is about 0. This applies to r1, r5, r9 and r13. The row bears on no version: it is weight-neuron pruning, not direction ablation.
